# `allOfMapToForEach`

Suggests using Effect.forEach instead of Effect.all over an effectful Array#map

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Style |
| Default severity | `suggestion` |
| Fixable | Yes |
| Effect versions | v3, v4 |
| Diagnostic codes | `TS377113` |
| Language Service name | `allOfMapToForEach` |
| Oxlint name | `effecttsgo/all-of-map-to-for-each` |

## Preview

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect"

declare const values: ReadonlyArray<number>

export const program = Effect.all(
/**
                       ^^^^^^^^^^ effecttsgo(all-of-map-to-for-each): `Effect.forEach` expresses this effectful array mapping more directly than `Effect.all` over `Array#map`.
*/
  values.map((value) => Effect.succeed(value + 1))
)
```
